newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold prices, volume jump on world trends.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold prices, volume jump on world trends.

text.p: Prices on the Istanbul Gold Exchange rose sharply in brisk trading on Tuesday, reflecting expectations of higher world values and the underlying weakness of the Turkish lira, dealers said.
Gold closed at $382.50 an ounce, up from Monday's $380.30, and at 1,208,300 lira per gram versus 1,201,500.
Volume more than tripled to 1,031 kilos from Monday's 285.

"Expectations of higher world prices and an awaited further fall of the Turkish lira (against the dollar) raised free market buying despite weak public demand at this time of the year," one bank dealer said.
The lira eased to 97,960 to the dollar from 97,700 at the opening despite central bank intervention, but was firmer on Monday's 98,100 close.
Dealers said the lira's fall in the afternoon prompted late purchasing on the gold exchange amid expectations the currency would continue to slide against the dollar on Wednesday due to excess cash.
Turnover was 721 kilos of gold in the morning session and 310 in the afternoon. Some 81 percent of total trade was in lira terms.
